layman_headline: Market fear is at extreme levels — patience is the smartest play right now.
layman_explanation: The crypto market is gripped by extreme fear with a score of 25 out of 100 and worsening day by day. Bitcoin is holding around $63,500 but faces a critical test at $65,000 before Friday's jobs data, which could send it lower to $60,000. The swing trade candidates available right now are either already overbought after big runs (like Bitway up 45% in a week), lacking reliable chart data, or in clear downtrends. None of them offer a setup worth risking capital on in this environment.
layman_action: Stay in cash and wait. The market mood is deteriorating, and Friday's US jobs data could create a much better buying opportunity if prices dip further. Don't chase anything that's already run up.
expert_reasoning: Per validated Rule #3, when Fear & Greed drops to 25 or below, the short-term outlook is genuinely ambiguous and the safest call is HOLD. Per Rule #7, early evidence suggests BTC tends to drift down another 1-4% when F&G is at this level. The candidate analysis: BTW has RSI 69 (overbought, our most reliable signal at 71% win rate says avoid), up 45.6% in 7 days with a terrible risk/reward of 0.29x. MON has a bearish chart bias of -0.70 and is below all MAs. AAVE is neutral but in a 5-day downtrend with -5.3% weekly. LDO is down 18% weekly with no chart data at all. The macro backdrop includes US-Japan yen intervention testing carry-trade fears and a first US spot BTC ETF closing due to dwindling inflows — both bearish signals. BTC dominance at 56.4% is hostile to altcoin positions. CryptoSlate's warning about BTC needing $65K before Friday or risking $60K adds urgency to staying sidelined.
